preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 10
preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::3]) and all(len(line.split()) == N for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::3])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains two integers N and K (1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5, 0 ≤ K ≤ 10^9), and the third line contains exactly N integers for array A, and the fourth line contains exactly N integers for array B.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= abs(int(x)) <= 10**5 for x in A) and all(0 <= abs(int(x)) <= 10**5 for x in B)
preconditions.description: All elements in arrays A and B satisfy 0 ≤ |A[i]|, |B[i]| ≤ 10^5.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T integers, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(int(stdout.split()[i]) == max(sum(A[j] * B[j] for j in range(N)) + sum(max(0, min(K, abs(B[j]))) * B[j] for j in range(N)), sum(A[j] * B[j] for j in range(N)) + sum(min(K, abs(B[j])) * B[j] for j in range(N)) if K > 0 else sum(A[j] * B[j] for j in range(N))) for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is the maximum possible interaction value (sum of A[i] * B[i]) after performing at most K operations (each operation increases or decreases an element of A by 1). The optimal strategy is to adjust each A[i] to be as close as possible to B[i] (if B[i] > 0) or as far as possible from B[i] (if B[i] < 0), using up to K operations in total.
